Stick-built vs. prefab ADUs: what actually differs

Both approaches can produce a good home. The difference is where the building is made, and that changes a few practical things.

Access

A prefab unit arrives on a truck and is often set by crane. That needs a wide path or open sky above the lot. A stick-built home is framed where it stands, so a narrow side yard or a locked gate matters much less.

Flexibility

On-site framing means room sizes, kitchens and details can change to suit the lot. Prefab plans are usually fixed in a factory, with less room to adapt.

Logistics

Delivered units add transport and crane costs. Stick-built homes add on-site construction time. Which is better for you depends on your lot, your schedule and your budget.
